min_stable_gain.conditions: noise gain 2 (G = +2 or G = -1) with the external compensation network (RC, CC, C1) and CF of Table 4; without compensation the datasheet states stability for gains above 15
min_stable_gain.datasheet_text: 'The AD8099 can be externally compensated down to a gain of 2 through the use of an RC network. Above gains of 15, no external compensation network is required.' (p15). 'In low gain configurations (less than 15), the AD8099 requires external compensation.' (p16). 'Custom external compensation, gain range -1, +2 to +10' (Features p1). 'Even though the AD8099 is not unity-gain stable, it can be configured to produce a net gain of +1 amplifier' by combining +2 and -1 (p22).
min_stable_gain.below_minimum: No guidance for noise gain below 2, for capacitive (TIA) feedback or for noise-gain shaping. CF is described as creating a zero to compensate the pole formed by the input capacitance (including stray) and RF, typical 0.5 to 1.5 pF (p16).
min_stable_gain.uncompensated_open_loop_check: DERIVED from Fig. 14: open-loop phase reaches -180 deg at about 480 MHz where |A| is about 19.5 dB (x9.4), so without CC a noise gain well above about 10 is needed; consistent with the 'above 15' statement.

tia_content_note: None. 'Optical electronics' and 'Preamplifiers', 'Receivers' are listed under Applications (p1); no transimpedance or photodiode example, figure or equation. Only the CF description (zero against input-capacitance/RF pole, 0.5-1.5 pF) is related.
application_guidance: Use Table 4 networks as starting points (p16-17). Compensation-pin area is very sensitive to parasitic capacitance: no trace at or near the CC pin when uncompensated; when compensated, make traces to CC pin, -Vs and between CC, C1, RC as wide as possible (p23). Clear ground/power planes under the pins (one SOIC pad can add 0.2 pF). Bypass: C2/C3 between both supplies, 0508 case for C3 and C5, 0.1 uF at the pins with electrolytics beside them. Use NP0 for CF (X7R drift of 0.23 pF over 100 C gives excessive peaking, Fig. 71). Solder the exposed paddle to ground. Noise model Fig. 74; offset model Fig. 75 (p21).
abs_max_and_input_protection: Supply 12.6 V; differential input +/-1.8 V; differential input current +/-10 mA; storage -65 to +125 C; operating -40 to +125 C; lead 300 C (10 s); junction 150 C (Table 3, p5). Antiparallel diode pairs (two series diodes each) clamp the differential input to about +/-1.8 V; ESD diodes to both rails; text says protection diodes handle 5 mA steady state, limit to 5 mA with a series resistor (p15).
other_notes: DISABLE pin (Table 5, p21): +/-5 V: -5 to +2.4 V disables, open enables, 4.3 to 5 V low input bias current; +5 V: 0 to 2.4 V disables. Turn-off 105 ns, turn-on 39 ns (+/-5 V) / 61 ns (+5 V); off isolation -61 dB at 1 MHz; enable-pin leakage 17/21 uA, DISABLE-pin leakage 35/44 uA. Offset vs temperature Fig. 53; bias vs temperature Figs. 54, 57.
inconsistencies: Differential input current: Table 3 +/-10 mA vs text p15 'protection diodes can handle 5 mA of steady state current ... limited to 5 mA or less'.
Slew rate at G = +2: Features 475 V/us, Table 1 470 V/us typ, Table 4 515 V/us (SOIC) / 475 V/us (LFCSP).
GBWP 3.8 GHz (Features, no conditions) vs closed-loop G x BW from Table 4: 3.2 GHz at G = +20, 5.5 GHz at G = +10 (with peaking), 2.55 GHz at G = +5.
Table 2 (+5 V single supply) repeats the operating range as '+/-5 typ, +/-6 max V'.
Table 2 output swing: RL = 1 kohm MIN equals TYP (1.2 to 3.8 V) and RL = 100 ohm TYP equals RL = 1 kohm TYP, while the RL = 100 ohm MIN is 1.5 to 3.5 V.
Bias-current cancellation: 'approximate factor of 60' (p21) and '< 200 nA' (p15) vs Table 1 -0.1 uA typ / -2 uA max.
Input capacitance 2 pF (tables) vs about 5.6-5.9 pF effective from the G = +2 input-impedance curve (Fig. 18); the curve includes the fixture.
Typical-characteristics default note references Figs. 63-66 while Table 1 references Figs. 60-66.
Table 4 component columns carry no units (ohm/pF inferred from the schematics).
Noise curves above about 100-150 MHz show a bump and then a steep fall below the white level, i.e. measurement roll-off; not usable above about 100 MHz.
